public_rationale: DeepSeek disclosed useful serving economics, but its quoted revenue and margin were hypothetical. Midjourney's founder asserted profitability without defining the accounting measure or attributing it to infrastructure operation. These are relevant qualifications to a broad no-evidence claim, but neither settles the narrower causal reading. An incomplete search also cannot establish that qualifying evidence did not exist.
limitations: The result depends on the meaning of profitable and the required causal connection.
Later disclosures cannot establish what evidence was public when the post appeared.
The dated source facts are retained as context rather than moved into the publication-day target period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is no evidence that AI labs running their own infrastructure makes anything profitable.
conditions: even if labs run their own infrastructure

statement.excerpt: AI labs may be able to run their own infrastructure and save some costs, but we have no evidence that this makes anything “profitable.”

from_speaker: AI labs may be able to run their own infrastructure
our_interpretation: This is a claim about the public evidence available when the post appeared, not a forecast or a claim that future profitability is impossible.
The target is the public evidence record as of 2026-06-02. Earlier disclosures can inform that record but are not automatically outcome observations dated to publication.
The plain reading requires evidence of realized profitability attributable to operating infrastructure, rather than merely a theoretical serving-margin calculation.
The words anything and profitable leave open whether the intended unit is an inference service or the whole lab. Both readings must be distinguished.
No accounting basis is stated, preventing a decisive monetary score under the specified rules.
May be able to is a concession, not a conditional forecast antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive examination of the public record at publication establishes the absence of evidence demonstrating realized profitability attributable to lab-operated infrastructure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A disclosure available by publication demonstrates realized profitability on a defined basis and credibly connects it to operating infrastructure, within the intended service or company scope.

evidence.locator: Statistics of DeepSeek's Online Service, hypothetical revenue calculation
evidence.explanation: DeepSeek provides infrastructure activity and a hypothetical revenue calculation, while explaining that actual revenue was lower. This is relevant evidence about serving economics, but does not demonstrate realized company profit or a causal effect of operating infrastructure.

evidence.locator: Keeping us in food and clothes, David Holz interview
evidence.explanation: The founder describes Midjourney as a self-funded research lab and asserts profitability. This weakens a broad reading that no lab had supplied any profitability evidence, but the interview does not establish infrastructure ownership, causal attribution or a defined profit measure.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A prepublication disclosure with defined realized profit, documented infrastructure operation and credible attribution would contradict the claim. Supporting an absence claim would require a sufficiently complete review of the relevant public record.
